title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: one ratio of predestination — Head and members alike
pass_a_gloss: There is one ratio of predestination both as regards the Head and the members, and as regards the members compared among themselves. That is: If the predestination of Christ to the office of Mediator and Savior was gratuitous, and not from foresight of merits, then much more ought our predestination to the benefit of salvation to be gratuitous. Further, If it is manifest that certain members of Christ were predestinated to eternal life without any respect to the condition of foresighted faith or perseverance, then the same is to be established concerning all the rest. For that predestination, as regards conditions presupposed or not presupposed, is uniform, is beyond doubt.
pass_b_english: One ratio of predestination — Head and members, and members among themselves. If Christ's predestination to Mediator and Savior was gratuitous, not from foresight of merits, then much more must ours to the benefit of salvation be gratuitous. And if some of Christ's members were clearly predestined to eternal life with no regard to foresighted faith or perseverance, the same holds for all the rest. Predestination is uniform as to whether conditions are presupposed or not — that is beyond doubt.
source_text: Unica est ratio praedestinationis tum quoad Caput et membra, tum quoad membra inter se collata. Hoc est: Si praedestinatio Christi ad officium Mediatoris et Salvatoris fuerit gratuita, et non ex praevisione meritorum, tum multo magis praedestinatio nostri ad beneficium salutis gratuita esse debet. Porro, Si manifestum sit quaedam Christi membra ad vitam aeternam absque ullo respectu ad praevisae fidei aut perseverantiae conditionem fuisse praedestinata, tum idem statuendum est de reliquis omnibus. Praedestinationem enim, quoad conditiones praerequisitas aut non praerequisitas, uniformem esse, extra dubium est.
